THIS CAUSE HAS COME ON TO BE HEARD on the Application of the Cook County
Treasurer and Ex-Officio County Collector of Cook County, Illinois, Defendant, appearing by
her attorney, the State's Attorney of Cook County, Illinois, and on the objection of Plaintiff,
appearing by its attorneys, Nichols Law, and both parties having agreed to settle this
objection pursuant to 35 ILCS 200/23-30. Based upon the following:
IL.       The 2021 assessed valuation of $182.484, before equalization, is excessive. The correct 2021
assessed valuation, before equalization, is $134,042.
2       Applying the applicable equalization factor of 3.0027% and the applicable tax rate of 6.697%
to the correct assessed valuation of $134.042 results in an equalized assessed valuation of
$402.489 and a correct tax of $26.954.69.
Applying the same equalization factor and tax rate to the excess assessed valuation in the amount
of $48.442 results in an equalized assessed valuation of $145.456 and excess payment of taxes in
the amount of $9,741.19.
3:     THE DEFENDANT IS HEREBY ORDERED TO refund to the Plaintiff the sum of $9.741.19, plus
statutory interest, constituting the excess amount of taxes paid under protest for the year 2021.
4.        The Defendant shall make appropriate notations of this order in the proper real estate tax warrant book,
and the County Clerk shall make appropriate notations of this order in the proper property tax
judgment, sale forfeiture and redemption record.
